basis: Inherited disruption of peptide or amine metabolism; no organ damage is consistent across this umbrella.
Non-IgE-mediated hypersensitivity commonly involving mast-cell activation; transient skin and airway reactions do not establish additional organ damage.
Malignancy of monocytic blood and marrow cells; skin, gingival and neurologic infiltration are not established here as affecting at least 30%.
Precursor B-cell leukemia/lymphoma affects blood and marrow; the lymphoma component supports the immune axis.
Peripheral sensorimotor axonal neuropathy; muscle wasting reflects denervation rather than a primary muscle disease.
Congenital eyelid inversion; associated corneal injury remains within the ocular axis.
Agenesis of olfactory bulbs and tracts causes congenital anosmia; smell belongs to the neurologic axis.
Pyrimidine metabolism defect; seizures, intellectual disability and developmental delay occur in 30-79%. Reduced hepatic enzyme activity alone is not liver damage.
Chronic infectious inflammation and scarring of the renal pelvis and kidney.
Central movement disorder causing dystonia, parkinsonism and bulbar dysfunction; dysphagia does not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
Peroxisomal disorder; hepatic failure, cerebral atrophy/seizures and ASD/PDA each reported in 1/1 patient. Cardiac frequency is uncertain given the tiny sample.
Craniofacial dysostosis, ear/hearing defects and eyelid coloboma define the syndrome; cleft palate affects 4/13 (~31%), supporting gastrointestinal involvement.
Congenital cleft involves the laryngeal airway and its separation from the upper digestive tract; recurrent infections are secondary complications.
Idiopathic organizing injury of pulmonary airspaces causes consolidation and restrictive dysfunction; infection or an autoimmune cause is not established.
Malignant neoplasm arising in cranial nerves; ocular or otologic locations apply only to particular subtypes.
IRGM-associated inflammatory bowel disease directly affects the intestine through an immune-mediated process.
Hydrocephalus and severe neurologic dysfunction define the disease; congenital adducted thumbs and fixed thumb contractures are major features (20/20).
Congenital impairment of brain growth with intellectual disability; short stature alone does not establish skeletal or endocrine disease.
M. xenopi predominantly causes chronic pulmonary infection; extrapulmonary disease is uncommon.
Tubulin-related developmental disorder defined by cortical, basal ganglia and corpus callosum malformations.
Usher type 1B is defined by sensorineural deafness, vestibular dysfunction and progressive rod-cone retinal degeneration.
Tyrosine metabolism defect with defining corneal disease and palmoplantar keratoderma; intellectual disability is reported in 80-99% by supplied HPO annotations.
Abnormal bowel motility impairs intestinal absorption and causes diarrhea; no other organ damage is inherent.
Listed constitutional deletion syndromes predominantly affect brain development or peripheral nerves; variable deletion extent prevents consistent additional organ labels.
CEL-related monogenic diabetes; exocrine pancreatic dysfunction affects most patients and is an intrinsic feature of MODY8.
